  MEDIUM   F1   2 forwarded ports are open to any source                                          -4
                nat/PREROUTING translates these ports to another host, and filter/FORWARD accepts
                them from any source; the rules of filter/INPUT do not apply: IPv4 51820/udp to
                192.168.1.20:51820 (via eth0); IPv4 8443/tcp to 192.168.1.50:443 (via eth0).
                nat/PREROUTING #3:  -i eth0 -p udp -m udp --dport 51820 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.168.1.20:51820
                nat/PREROUTING #1:  -i eth0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 8443 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.168.1.50:443
                fix  Each of these ports is translated by its rule in nat/PREROUTING and then passes
                     filter/FORWARD, not filter/INPUT. If only known clients need a port, add their
                     sources (-s <trusted-cidr>) to its rule or to the FORWARD rule that accepts its
                     traffic. In FORWARD the packet has the translated address and port; match the
                     port that the clients use with '-m conntrack --ctorigdstport PORT --ctdir
                     ORIGINAL'.
